canonical_question: Does the significant drop in the work-hardening exponent from 0.2732 to 0.1199 suggest a transition in deformation mechanisms, such as from cross-slip to climb, at elevated temperatures?

question_variants.question: Does the significant drop in the work-hardening exponent from 0.2732 to 0.1199 suggest a transition in deformation mechanisms, such as from cross-slip to climb, at elevated temperatures?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The paper reports the drop in the work-hardening exponent but does not explicitly link this change to a transition between cross-slip and climb mechanisms.

answers.answer: The data shows the work-hardening exponent decreased from 0.2732 (RT) to 0.1199 (900°C), but the text does not propose or confirm a mechanism transition from cross-slip to climb.
answers.boundary_limitation: No explicit discussion of cross-slip or climb mechanisms.
evidence_spans: The microstructure of the homogenized NbTaTiV refractory HEA was characterized, using the scanning electron microscopy (SEM) backscattered electron (BSE) technique, as shown in Fig. 1A . A typical simple solid-solution HEA microstructure with grain sizes of 200 to 400 μm was identified without the presence of secondary phases or elemental segregations.

The chemical composition of the sample was verified (using the point energy-dispersive x-ray spectroscopy analysis) to be Nb 23.8 Ta 25.5 Ti 24.9 V 25.8 , indicating a homogeneous elemental distribution in a nearly equiatomic percentage.
The measured ND patterns of the bulk samples, as illustrated in Fig. 1B , confirm the single BCC solid solution at RT and elevated temperatures.
